scope: read-only source review of actual extracted Opus pure core and root-thread integration; no new physics or tests in this review
verdict: No blocker found for proceeding to the predeclared real-physics validation; does not assert the new interaction passes physical acceptance.
verified_by_reading: All inputs validated before intent memory changes; active ordinary release/reverse retains current direction.
Explicit cancel and new controller-failure edge enter release barrier; sticky failure does not re-lock on every tick.
Barrier release frame never starts a new tap, and active barrier continues safe cancellation.
Mode inhibition clears repetition and prevents delayed start until real release.
Same-poll A/D PRESS is consumed once; X PRESS has a separate latch so a same-poll X tap still cancels.
A+D physical conflict is distinguished from two released keys.
After reset sampled_after_reset=False prevents synthesized neutral input from clearing the barrier.
Old raw operator held direction is logged separately from resolved direction sent to unchanged drive.
GUI accepted jump/active side remain mutually guarded; pending jump during direct active drive remains safe-abort, without delayed jump.
Default side_input_mode remains release_abort until real-physics commit-cycle validation is complete.
limits: Physical cancellation and handoff continue to rely on unchanged side controller safety gates; this source review does not independently rerun them.
Core candidate includes a local cancel_reason validation fix relative to the raw Opus response; the original should not be described as passing unchanged.
